title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change

key_patterns.name: Multiplex network with heterogeneous degrees
key_patterns.description: Family layers are small and dense, work/school are moderate, community layers are larger and more diffuse; overall degrees are right-skewed.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific structure determines contact opportunities and the strength of social influence on mask adoption.

key_patterns.name: Directed edges with partial reciprocity
key_patterns.description: Adjacency lists are directed; not all ties are mutual. Reciprocity varies by layer (family highest, community lowest).
key_patterns.relevance: Influence can be asymmetric; decision to symmetrize affects effective degree and cascade potential.

key_patterns.name: Age/occupation mixing
key_patterns.description: Students primarily connect in the school/work layer; workers connect in the work layer; family spans ages; community shows mild homophily by age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Mixing patterns drive who influences whom; layer-specific mixing constraints should guide edge construction or filtering.

key_patterns.name: Initial mask-wearing heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Initial adopters are unevenly distributed across agents; prevalence varies by age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Starting conditions affect early diffusion trajectories; seeding should mirror observed heterogeneity.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception variability
key_patterns.description: risk_perception spans 0–1 and is likely unimodal or mildly right-skewed; suitable for Beta distribution fitting.
key_patterns.relevance: Maps to susceptibility thresholds; higher risk perception generally increases adoption propensity.

key_patterns.name: Temporal inertia in mask-wearing
key_patterns.description: Strong state persistence: P(mask_t=1 | mask_{t-1}=1) >> P(mask_t=1 | mask_{t-1}=0).
key_patterns.relevance: Behavior exhibits momentum; calibration must include persistence parameters (on- and off-durations).

key_patterns.name: Information exposure effect
key_patterns.description: received_info on day t (or t-1) increases adoption probability among previously unmasked agents.
key_patterns.relevance: Information acts as an exogenous driver and/or output of a diffusion process; calibrate its incremental effect separately from peer influence.

key_patterns.name: Degree–adoption linkage
key_patterns.description: Agents with higher total degree show different adoption hazards (often higher adoption due to more exposure, but can vary by layer weights).
key_patterns.relevance: Centrality heterogeneity can accelerate or dampen diffusion; important for targeting and scenario testing.

key_distributions.name: Layer-specific degree distributions
key_distributions.description: Empirical distributions of degrees in family, work_school, and community layers computed from social_network.json (or degree targets from agent_attributes.csv).
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L: mean_deg_L, sd_deg_L, p50_deg_L, p90_deg_L, max_deg_L; optionally fit a Negative Binomial with (r_L, p_L).

key_distributions.name: Total degree distribution
key_distributions.description: Distribution of deduplicated all-layer degrees per agent (social_network.json['all']).
key_distributions.parameters: mean_deg_all, sd_deg_all, tail index (Pareto alpha if heavy tail), Gini coefficient for degree inequality.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.description: Distribution of risk_perception ∈ [0,1] across agents (agent_attributes.csv). Fit a Beta distribution.
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(a, b) fit via method-of-moments or MLE; also report mean_risk and sd_risk.

key_distributions.name: Initial mask prevalence
key_distributions.description: Share of agents initially wearing a mask (agent_attributes.initial_mask_wearing or train_data day 0).

key_distributions.name: Information arrival rate
key_distributions.description: Daily probability an agent receives info (train_data.received_info). May be overdispersed across agents.
key_distributions.parameters: lambda_info = mean(received_info); across-agent variability: var_info_rate; optionally fit Beta-Binomial (alpha_info, beta_info).

key_distributions.name: State transition probabilities
key_distributions.description: Daily transition probabilities between masked and unmasked states (train_data).
key_distributions.parameters: p_on_noinfo = P(Mt=1|Mt-1=0, info_t=0); p_on_info = P(Mt=1|Mt-1=0, info_t=1); p_off = P(Mt=0|Mt-1=1); duration_on ~ Geometric(p_off); duration_off ~ Geometric(p_on_noinfo).

key_distributions.name: Reciprocity and clustering
key_distributions.description: Per-layer reciprocity and clustering from social_network.json after symmetrization choice.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception associated with higher probability of initial_mask_wearing.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via logistic regression: logit(P(mask=1)) = β0 + β1*risk_perception (+ controls). Expect β1 > 0 (medium to strong).

key_relationships.relationship: Information on day t increases adoption on day t.
key_relationships.strength: Incremental odds ratio OR_info = exp(β_info) > 1; estimate from train_data (medium to strong).
High; estimate p_off and p_on_noinfo from transition counts.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher fraction of masked neighbors increases adoption hazard, strongest in family layer.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via multi-layer weighted exposure model; expect family > work_school > community (medium).

key_relationships.relationship: Adoption probability correlates with total degree due to increased exposures; nonlinear at high degrees.
key_relationships.strength: Low to medium; verify via partial dependence controlling for risk_perception.

key_relationships.relationship: Students have higher work_school degrees; retirees have lower work_school degrees, higher community/family.
key_relationships.strength: High; use to constrain network wiring or validate social_network.json.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher reciprocity relates to stronger local clustering of behavior (Moran’s I).
key_relationships.strength: Medium; diagnostic for whether to symmetrize edges.

num_agents.notes: Ensure alignment of agent_id domains across files; drop or add isolates as needed.

degree_sequences_by_layer.value: Empirical degree sequences per layer from social_network.json (post choice: directed vs symmetrized)
degree_sequences_by_layer.notes: If constructing networks from targets (agent_attributes.csv), match target degrees via configuration model per layer with mixing constraints.

reciprocity_by_layer.value: recip_family, recip_work_school, recip_community (compute from directed lists)
reciprocity_by_layer.notes: Use to decide whether to treat influence as directed; if symmetrizing, report pre- and post-values.

clustering_by_layer.notes: Compute on undirected version; match approximately in synthetic rewiring.

mixing_matrices.value: P(contact | age_group_i → age_group_j) and P(contact | occupation_i → occupation_j) per layer
mixing_matrices.notes: Estimate empirical mixing; enforce during edge wiring in synthetic networks.

layer_influence_weights.source: Expert prior; to be calibrated against train_data adoption dynamics
layer_influence_weights.notes: Relative weights in aggregating neighbor influence; calibrate to match adoption responsiveness across layers if layer exposures can be inferred.

interaction_rates_per_layer_per_day.source: Expert prior; adjust to match contact frequency assumptions
interaction_rates_per_layer_per_day.notes: Expected number of salient interactions per agent per day by layer; scales the amount of social exposure.

initial_mask_prevalence.notes: Use agent_attributes for seeding unless time series provides an earlier baseline.

p_adopt_no_info.notes: Compute from transitions; serves as baseline adoption absent info and peer effects.

p_adopt_with_info.notes: Captures incremental effect of info on same day (can also include received_info_{t-1}).

p_drop.notes: Controls adherence decay; can be modeled as constant or dependent on info/peers.

peer_influence_coefficient.value: β_peer (log-odds increase per unit weighted neighbor_mask_share)
peer_influence_coefficient.source: Calibrate using train_data with simulated exposure or using social_network.json + observed neighbor states if available
peer_influence_coefficient.notes: Use logistic model: logit(P(adopt)) = β0 + β_info*info + β_peer*E_t + β_risk*risk + interactions; E_t = Σ_L w_L * masked_share_L.

risk_susceptibility_scaler.notes: Maps risk_perception into threshold/susceptibility: θ_i = θ0 - α*risk_i; start α=1.0.

exogenous_noise_flip.notes: Small probability of random state change to account for unobserved shocks.

external_info_rate.notes: If modeling info as diffusion, treat this as baseline exogenous rate.

peer_info_transmission_prob_per_contact.source: Calibrate so simulated received_info prevalence and clustering match train_data
peer_info_transmission_prob_per_contact.notes: Use multiplex independent cascade for info spread; constrain τ_family ≥ τ_work_school ≥ τ_community.

info_effect_size_on_adoption.notes: Plug into adoption logistic model; can allow lagged effects β_info_lag.

info_memory_decay_days.source: Assumption based on train_data definition (daily flag)
info_memory_decay_days.notes: If evidence of lagged effects, extend to 2–3 days with decay.

warmup_days.notes: Set >0 if initializing from agent_attributes but validating against later train_data window.

observed_variables.notes: Assumed measured without error; if not, add observation noise.

target_moments.notes: Use as calibration and validation targets.

preprocessing_steps.step: Align agent_id across files and restrict to intersection set
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure consistent population across attributes, network, and time series.
Check agent_attributes total_connections equals sum of layer-specific degrees; flag anomalies.
Compute reciprocity; choose directed influence or symmetrize adjacency; construct undirected edges if required.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute per-layer degrees, clustering, and mixing matrices
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Summarize topology for configuration and synthetic network generation if needed.
From train_data, create mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, received_info_{t-1}, and transition indicators.
Compute p_on_noinfo, p_on_info, p_off and duration distributions as initial calibration targets.

preprocessing_steps.step: Join risk_perception and demographics to time series
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Enable heterogeneous effect estimation and stratified validation.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a staged (hybrid frequentist + simulation-based) approach: (1) Estimate direct-from-data parameters: initial_mask_prevalence, p_on_noinfo, p_on_info, p_off, lambda_info, Beta(a,b) for risk_perception, degree/mixing summaries. (2) Fit a logistic model on train_data: logit(P(Mt=1)) = β0 + γ*Mt-1 + β_info*received_info_t + β_risk*risk_i + β_demo*X_i. This yields β_info, persistence γ, and baseline. (3) In the agent-based simulation, incorporate network exposure E_i,t = Σ_L w_L * masked_share among neighbors per layer and add β_peer for peer effects. Calibrate β_peer, layer weights w_L, and peer info transmission τ_L via simulation-based optimization (e.g., ABC-SMC or Bayesian optimization) to match observed prevalence trajectory, transition rates, and (if available) spatial/network clustering of adoption. (4) If modeling info diffusion endogenously, match simulated received_info rates and their temporal autocorrelation to train_data. Prioritize identifiability by fixing either β_peer or τ_L initially, then release both.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out a time window (e.g., last 20% of days) and validate: (a) Aggregate prevalence: RMSE/MAE between simulated and observed daily mask prevalence. (b) Transition rates: compare p_on and p_off by day and by strata (age_group, occupation, degree quintiles). (c) Micro-level trajectories: Hamming distance or dynamic Brier score for agent-level mask states. (d) Network patterns: if neighbor states over time are available or reconstructable, validate clustering (Moran’s I) and community-level prevalence. Perform k-fold time-slice cross-validation and sensitivity analysis over key parameters (β_peer, w_L, τ_L).

file_summaries.semantic_summary:
- Overall data structure and type:
  - Flat CSV table; one row per agent.
  - Primary key: agent_id (integer, unique).
  - Columns/types:
    - age (int), age_group (categorical string), occupation (categorical string)
    - risk_perception (float 0–1)
    - initial_mask_wearing (boolean)
    - family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections, total_connections (integers)
  - total_connections equals the sum of the three layer-specific connection counts.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No nested records or explicit edge lists; relationships are implicit via degree counts per social layer.
  - Implies a multiplex network with three layers: family, work/school, community. Each agent has a target degree in each layer.
  - Occupation and age_group suggest mixing constraints within layers (e.g., students in school layer; workers in work layer), but this is not explicitly encoded—must be inferred during network construction.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agent initialization:
    - Create one agent per row with attributes: age/age_group, occupation, risk_perception, initial_mask_wearing.
    - initial_mask_wearing sets the agent’s starting behavior state.
    - risk_perception provides a baseline propensity or threshold for adopting mask-wearing.
  - Network generation:
    - Construct three layer-specific networks matching each agent’s degree targets (family, work/school, community); total degree emerges from multiplex union.
    - Apply optional homophily/mixing rules using age_group and occupation to wire edges plausibly (e.g., students with students in school, workers with workers in work).
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Social influence on mask adoption should be computed per layer, allowing different influence strengths (e.g., family > work/school > community) and aggregated to update behavior.
    - Age_group and occupation can modulate influence weights or contact frequency; risk_perception modulates susceptibility to peer influence.
  - Data checks/notes:
    - Validate total_connections consistency; handle any anomalies (e.g., young ages with work connections) per modeling assumptions rather than strict real-world constraints.

- Overall data structure and type
  - JSON object mapping agent IDs (as strings) to adjacency lists (arrays of integers).
  - Each agent record contains four arrays: family, work_school, community, and all.
  - Topology is static (no timestamps); IDs appear to range 0–999.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - family, work_school, community represent distinct network layers (tie contexts).
  - all is the deduplicated union of contacts across the three layers for that agent.
  - Edges are listed from the focal agent to others; reciprocity is not guaranteed (i.e., directed adjacency lists). Convert to undirected if needed by symmetrizing.
  - Layer sizes suggest stronger, smaller family networks; moderate work/school; larger community ties.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agents: each top-level key is an agent; initialize per-agent state (e.g., mask_wearing ∈ {0,1}, adoption threshold, susceptibility).
  - Network layers: model as a multiplex graph; assign interaction frequency/weight and influence strength per layer (e.g., family > work_school > community).
  - Contact process: per timestep, sample interactions from each layer according to layer-specific rates; or use all for unlayered simulations.
  - Influence/adoption: compute likelihood of adopting/maintaining mask-wearing from neighbors’ states, weighted by layer; support directed influence unless symmetrized.
  - Seeding and interventions: select initial adopters; target layers (e.g., workplace campaigns) by adjusting weights or probabilities within work_school edges.
  - Metrics: use all to compute overall degree/centrality; use layer-specific degrees for targeted strategies.
  - Data hygiene: verify that neighbors exist in the node set; ensure all equals union(family, work_school, community); handle potential asymmetry if undirected behavior is desired.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

- Overall data structure and type:
  - Rectangular CSV; long-format panel (time-series) data.
  - Columns:
    - day: integer, discrete daily time step.
    - agent_id: integer, agent identifier.
    - wearing_mask: boolean, agent’s behavioral state at that day.
    - received_info: boolean, whether the agent received mask-related information that day.
  - Composite key: (agent_id, day). No missing nested structures.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Temporal dependency within each agent_id across day (state transitions over time).
  - wearing_mask is the outcome state; received_info is a potential driver/exposure.
  - No explicit network topology or interactions between agents included; any contagion/peer effects are implicit and must be modeled or inferred externally.
  - Enables derivation of transition events (e.g., adopt, cease) via lagged states per agent.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Entities: One agent per agent_id with state variables:
    - mask_state ∈ {true, false}
    - info_state ∈ {true, false} (possibly transient/per-day)
  - Time step: daily scheduler aligned with day.
  - Calibration targets:
    - Baseline transition probabilities P(mask_t | mask_{t-1}) to capture inertia/relapse.
    - Incremental effect of information P(mask_t | mask_{t-1}, received_info_t or received_info_{t-1}).
    - Durations of adherence and rates of switching absent info (spontaneous adoption/cessation).
  - Interactions:
    - Use received_info events as exogenous inputs or as outcomes of network diffusion; calibrate info-spread parameters (e.g., per-edge transmission) so simulated received_info rates match observed frequencies.
    - Initialize agents’ day 0 states from data when available; validate simulated trajectories against per-agent adoption curves and aggregate prevalence over time.
  - Missing elements to be supplied by the simulation:
    - Network topology (e.g., ER/WS/BA) and peer influence rules.
    - Any heterogeneity beyond agent_id (no demographics provided).
